label: Mid/late original-phase input from a letter set (l,k,y,n,v,r,j,a,h,2,c,i) after a prefix with 2+ of {z,0,w,b,m,u}
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (99.5% of mass), at positions t>=3 (rate peaks at orig_idx 5-6), and essentially silent at t<=2, on <DEL> (0.4% of mass) and throughout the copy phase. The current input matters: l and k fire most (about 5x lift), then y, n, v, r, j, a, h, 2, c, and i is weak. Activations are mostly on the first occurrence of the token (90% of mass). The prefix also matters: it fires more when earlier inputs include z, 0, w, b, m, u (the first_tok and prev2_tok lifts are 2-4x). Requiring at least 2 such earlier tokens gives dev F1 0.36 (P 0.25, R 0.65, mass 0.75). Requiring at least 3 raises precision to about 0.40 but recall drops to 0.25, which suggests the activation grows with how much of this context has built up. Precision stays low because many steps that match the predicate are inactive, so this looks like a graded, hidden-state-dependent mix of token identity and prefix composition, not a clean rule. Adding more conditions did not help.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=6: l, k, y, v; t=5: k, l, y, v; t=7: k, l, y, n) and the first original token (most: z, w, 0, b, m, u; least: v, k, r, l); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=11, t=5.
